neighbours.label: wind, air pressure and altitude as conditions (windy, winds, windproof, high altitude, low oxygen) — the airy side of a weather/exposure distinction whose other pole is dryness/moisture
fire: Bring a warm hat because the ridge gets very windy after lunch.
Strong winds knocked down several trees along the coast last night.
Climbers often feel dizzy at high altitude until their bodies adjust.
A sudden drop in air pressure usually means a storm is on its way.
Sailors waited two days in port for the gusty winds to calm down.
Wear a windproof shell over your fleece when cycling in the hills.
The coffee grows at high altitude on the slopes of the volcano.
Low barometric pressure can make some people's joints ache.
quiet: Bring a warm hat because the ridge gets very cold after sunset.
Heavy snow closed several roads along the coast last night.
Climbers often feel tired in the heat until their bodies adjust.
A sudden drop in temperature usually means the first frost is near.
Sailors waited two days in port for the thick fog to lift.
Wear a light shirt under your fleece when cycling in the hills.
The coffee grows in rich soil on the slopes of the volcano.
Cold, damp mornings can make some people's joints ache.

notes: Card: + peaks on 'wind'proof, ' windy', ' winds', ' altitude', ' pressure', hyp'ox'ia, 'short-day' conditions. The - pole is ' dry'/' moisture'/' fungal'. Output suppresses rain/wet words. Near misses keep weather/outdoor topic but mention rain, heat, cold or sun, not wind, pressure or altitude.
